A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ChronoGS method and ChronoScene dataset. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary material support reliable comparison, including matching renumbered and relocated content.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction experiments on real and synthetic ChronoScene scenes, comparisons with baselines, and component, feature-dimension, and initialization ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds baseline comparisons and ChronoGS results on WAT, CL-Splats, and NeuSC's 5Pointz scene.

M1.justification: The unified anchor scaffold, invariant/local/global features, temporal interpolation, opacity activation, Gaussian decoding, and optimization remain unchanged. Expanded descriptions of voxelization and visibility filtering repeat details already present in v1's supplement.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates exclusively on ChronoScene. V2 adds WAT, the CL-Splats real-world benchmark, and NeuSC's 5Pointz scene, extending coverage to other continual-rendering and appearance-evolution settings. ChronoScene's 12 scenes and 8,891 images are retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds NeuSC and CLNeRF alongside all five retained baselines. New Tables 9–11 introduce further comparisons including NeRF, MEIL-NeRF, GsEditor, CL-NeRF, CL-Splats, NeRFW, HaNeRF, and time-conditioned variants. CLNeRF and CL-NeRF are distinct cited methods.

E3.justification: The added WAT comparison reports PSNR and SSIM, while the added CL-Splats and 5Pointz comparisons also report LPIPS. Existing ChronoScene evaluation, period averaging, and the stated 40k-iteration budget remain unchanged. Benchmark-specific splits and training procedures for the new comparisons are not detailed.

E4.justification: The component ablations, feature-dimension sweeps, initialization study, per-period training comparison, and temporal-interpolation examples are retained. Appendix C adds benchmark comparisons, without a distinct new ablation, robustness test, or error analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2's use of 'significantly' in discussing performance is not accompanied by statistical testing.

E6.justification: V2 adds NeuSC/CLNeRF scores throughout Table 1 and three external-benchmark result tables. ChronoGS reports PSNR 28.31 on WAT, 32.03 on CL-Splats, and 19.35 on 5Pointz, where NeuSC reports 21.32. Table 1 also revises Overstreet PSNR from 22.46 to 22.66, matching unchanged Table 2.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 and the supplementary grid-occupancy definition retain the same mathematical content. No theorem, proof, derivation, or substantive formal assumption is introduced or revised.

C1.justification: The introduction and conclusion narrow the priority claim from first addressing and benchmarking multi-period 3D reconstruction to first reconstructing it within a unified, differentiable Gaussian-splatting framework. V2 also removes the assertion that ChronoScene is the only available benchmark coupling geometric and appearance evolution.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly assumes within-period changes are small. Appendix C attributes performance differences to incremental-change versus fixed-geometry appearance settings and acknowledges lower performance than NeuSC. Section 3.2 removes the earlier empirical assertion that opacity gating stabilizes training.

D1.justification: The introduction newly discloses that periods are manually defined using metadata or prior knowledge. Hardware, software versions, learning rates, densification schedules, feature dimensions, and code/data access information otherwise remain unchanged; an actual preprocessing change is not established.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 becomes 'Long-Term Scene Evolution Modeling' and substantially expands positioning around historical scene chronology, temporal ordering, time-lapse reconstruction, and continual adaptation. Added literature includes CLNeRF and CL-Splats, supporting a more specific distinction between ChronoGS and prior temporal-scene research.

P1.justification: V2 locally rewrites related work and the method introduction, standardizes period terminology, and corrects wording. It reorganizes supplementary sections as A–E, adds separate supplementary references and acknowledgments, and updates affiliation/corresponding-author information. Most narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 is expanded and reformatted, and Tables 9–11 are added. Diagram labels and several captions receive limited edits, while appendix figures move with the added material. Existing qualitative panels and point-cloud visualizations are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses important gaps in v1's empirical coverage and positioning: evaluation expands beyond the authors' benchmark, directly relevant chronological and continual methods enter the comparisons, and the novelty claim becomes more precise. Reporting the NeuSC shortfall also clarifies performance boundaries. These changes substantially strengthen the paper's evidential basis, although sparse protocol details for the new benchmarks still limit reproducibility.
